title: Work IQ: granular MCP policies to restrict platforms, workloads and operations
summary: Hold: the briefing says workload-restriction controls are undocumented, but Microsoft documents workload selection for individual agents in Copilot Studio. Narrow that absence to tenant-level granular policies, and distinguish the policy page's blocked-write default from Copilot Studio documentation that describes writes as enabled subject to organizational policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans granular policies restricting MCP access to trusted platforms, workloads and supported operations.
claims.quote: Provide granular policies that restrict MCP access to trusted platforms, workloads, and supported operations.

claims.where: What's changing; Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn has no documentation describing the planned granular tenant policies or their specific per-operation control surface.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state of the planned granular policy control is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "default" "granular". Read roadmap description and policy-governance-mcp; neither states whether the planned granular policies enforce restrictions on arrival. The documented mutation default concerns current MCP policy, not the planned control.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The current tenant policy is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools.
In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation for the current Work IQ MCP tenant policy switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "graph"; "Work IQ" "policy" "API" "update"; "Work IQ" "policy" "PowerShell". Read policy-governance-mcp; no setting operation or reference surfaced.

claims.claim: The planned tenant-level per-platform, per-workload, per-agent or per-operation policy controls have no documented UI or API.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "granular" "policies"; "Work IQ" "policy" "graph"; "Work IQ" "policy" "API" "update". Read policy-governance-mcp and add-work-iq; maker workload selection is not this tenant policy.

claims.where: controls[0].scope and note; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented initial policy control is tenant-level and applies across the tenant.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. ... When you turn on the policy, it applies across the tenant and helps control MCP tool access at request time.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The currently documented tenant-administrator policy choice is turning Work IQ MCP policy on or off.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: The Work IQ policy layer uses Rego.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.claim: Rego is the policy language from Open Policy Agent.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.claim: The policy layer evaluates each MCP tool request at request time and can allow or deny it.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.claim: The policy page says more granular controls and policy templates might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are not part of the initial policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: What's changing; Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Mutation operations are blocked by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety.
claims.fix: Attribute the default explicitly to the MCP policy page and add: 'The Copilot Studio Work IQ page describes write operations as on by default, subject to organizational permissions and policies; verify the effective behavior in your client and tenant.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq, which states 'Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.'

claims.where: What's changing; Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Mutation operations include create, update, delete and actions that modify data such as sending email.
claims.quote: This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly linked this roadmap item to the later controls mentioned on the policy governance page.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "granular" "policies". Read roadmap record and policy-governance-mcp; the record describes planned restrictions, while Learn mentions possible later controls without identifying this roadmap item.

claims.where: What's changing; Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not defined trusted platforms or how the planned policies identify them.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "trusted platforms"; Work IQ MCP granular policies trusted platforms workloads operations default preview policy governance. Read roadmap record, Work IQ overview, MCP overview and policy-governance-mcp; none defines platform trust or identification.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP provides generic resource-path tools for reading and changing Microsoft 365 data, subject to policy.
claims.quote: It provides tools that enable agents to read, create, update, and delete entities across Microsoft 365 and connected enterprise systems

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tools access mail, calendar, files, people, chat and sites.
claims.quote: provide direct access to Microsoft 365 data (mail, calendar, files, people, chat, and sites) and the ability to act on that data.

claims.claim: Policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: The policy page lists data access scope among default guardrail control areas.
claims.quote: Data access scope | Which Microsoft 365 resource paths MCP tools can access

claims.claim: The policy page lists bounded collection reads among default guardrail control areas.
claims.quote: Data retrieval limits | Whether collection reads are bounded to reduce large-scale data extraction risk

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet
claims.claim: Controls that restrict by platform or workload are not documented yet, leaving tenant policy and user permissions as today's boundary.
claims.quote: You can remove workloads your agent doesn't need from its Work IQ configuration. ... The agent no longer uses the workloads you remove through Work IQ.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'Controls that restrict by platform or workload' with 'The planned tenant-level granular policy controls that restrict by platform or workload are not yet documented.' The existing Copilot Studio maker workload selection is a different control, so do not describe workload restrictions generally as undocumented.

claims.claim: Policy supplements rather than replaces Entra authentication, OAuth permissions and user permissions.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Policy evaluates the requested resource path.
claims.quote: Path | The resource path being accessed, such as a mail, calendar, Teams, file, or people resource path

claims.claim: Policy evaluates the requested operation.
claims.quote: Operation | The requested operation, such as read, create, update, delete, action, or function

claims.claim: Policy evaluates request content.
claims.quote: Request content | Details in the request body or query parameters, when applicable

claims.claim: Policy evaluates tenant context.
claims.quote: User and tenant context | Information used to apply tenant-level governance rules

claims.where: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Tenant policy can deny a request despite successful authentication and the required app OAuth permission.
claims.quote: an MCP request can fail because of tenant policy even when the user is authenticated and the app has the required OAuth permission.

claims.claim: Microsoft tells developers to treat policy-denied responses as governance decisions.
claims.quote: Treat policy-denied responses as governance decisions, not transient failures to retry automatically.

claims.claim: Work IQ cost can be managed in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage and can be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The policy settings require an account permitted to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.

claims.claim: Learn names no specific role for managing the MCP tenant policy settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy manage tenant settings administrator role permissions. Read policy-governance-mcp and enable-work-iq; the former names no policy-editing role, and the latter requires Global Administrator for one-time provisioning.

claims.claim: When policy settings are missing, Microsoft advises checking tenant access to Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Work IQ MCP policy settings, check that your tenant has access to Work IQ MCP

claims.claim: When policy settings are missing, Microsoft advises checking the administrator's permissions.
claims.quote: check that your tenant has access to Work IQ MCP and that your admin account has the required permissions.

claims.claim: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically at first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Policy configuration before any MCP use can fail because the service principal has not been provisioned.
claims.quote: such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs tenant administrators to Enable your tenant for Work IQ to provision a missing service principal.
claims.quote: Tenant administrators can provision it by following the steps in Enable your tenant for Work IQ.

claims.claim: The policy page discusses experiences configuring policy settings and updating editable policies.

claims.claim: The policy page describes toggle values such as Allowed and Disallowed.

claims.claim: The policy governance page itself names no endpoint or cmdlet for modifying policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "API" "update"; "Work IQ" "policy" "PowerShell". Read policy-governance-mcp in full, including Developer considerations; it describes editable settings and validation but gives no endpoint or cmdlet.

claims.claim: Migration guidance says tenant-wide blocking stops Work IQ MCP for the entire tenant.

claims.claim: The migration page does not give the navigation path for tenant-wide blocking.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy settings Microsoft Graph beta API PowerShell Allowed Disallowed policy update. Read migrate-retrieval-api: Roll back mentions tenant-wide blocking and Troubleshoot names the Agent Tools registry, but neither gives the path.

claims.claim: Policy approval does not guarantee success because resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's permissions.
claims.quote: Policy approval doesn't guarantee the operation succeeds. If policy allows an MCP tool request, the underlying resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: No source states that the planned granular-policy rollout automatically changes existing tenant behavior.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "default" "granular". Read roadmap record and policy-governance-mcp; neither describes an automatic behavior change for the planned granular policies.
